content: BIBREF22 defines three psycholinguistic diagnostics for language models and applies them in a case study to BERT. Negation is examined using a dataset of 72 simple sentences querying for category membership. A supplementary dataset of 16 sentences queries again for the "to be" relation only but including more natural sentence structure. Our work covers 51,329 negated statements covering a wide range of topics and relations. In the SQuAD based dataset we cover more natural language in terms of context and relation. In contrast to BIBREF22, we do not see a reliable preference of the true completions to false in the more natural negated statements.
